questions.q: In what year was the Bahmani Kingdom founded, and who was its founder?
questions.a: It was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah. A wrong answer here suggests the student is mixing up dates or names with other historical periods, indicating they need to re-read the timeline introduction.

questions.q: What is the relationship between the Bahmani Kingdom and the five Deccan Sultanates?
questions.a: The Bahmani Kingdom broke up, and the five Deccan Sultanates were the smaller kingdoms that formed from that break. A wrong answer reveals the student thinks these were five separate, unrelated groups that never belonged to a single kingdom.

questions.q: If you were drawing a map of the year 1530, would you draw one Bahmani Kingdom or five separate sultanates? Why?
questions.a: You would draw five because the Bahmani Kingdom ended in 1527. A wrong answer shows the student failed to note the end date of the original kingdom.

questions.q: Compare the structure of the Deccan region before 1347 and after 1527.
questions.a: Before 1347, the region was part of the Delhi Sultanate; after 1527, it was divided into five independent sultanates. A wrong answer reveals confusion about the transition of power in the Deccan.

questions.q: Is it accurate to say the Deccan Sultanates existed throughout the entire time the Bahmani Kingdom existed?
questions.a: No, the Sultanates only emerged after the Bahmani Kingdom collapsed in 1527. A wrong answer implies the student does not understand the chronological order of these events.

questions.q: Create a mnemonic or a simple list to remember the five Deccan Sultanates.
questions.a: A good answer would be a memory hook like "B-A-B-B-G" (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar, Golconda). A poor answer lists incorrect names or misses several, showing a lack of engagement with the specific regional names provided.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Bahmani Kingdom was an ______ state established in the Deccan in 1347, which later split into five regional powers known as the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar, and Golconda) in 1527.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever seen a large piece of clay split into several smaller, ______ pieces?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify the transition from a single kingdom to five smaller sultanates and correctly name the five Deccan Sultanates.
